instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Insurtech MGA underwriting parametric weather insurance for smallholder farmers in Southern Europe. Payouts are triggered automatically by satellite-verified rainfall deficits or frost events, leveraging proprietary geospatial data to manage risk efficiently across Portugal and Spain. The company is rapidly scaling its operations while navigating complex cross-border compliance requirements.
answers.pastInitiatives: Our engineering team adopted an agile methodology last year, moving from waterfall-style quarterly releases to 2-week sprints with continuous deployment. This reduced our release cycle time by 60% and improved cross-functional collaboration. However, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are still adapting to the faster cadence, leading to occasional misalignment between product delivery and market readiness.
answers.strategicGoals: Customer retention has declined from 92% to 84% over the past 18 months, primarily among our mid-tier and enterprise segments. Exit interviews consistently cite product stagnation and poor digital self-service tools as reasons for leaving. We need to urgently modernize our customer-facing technology and proactively address the specific pain points driving churn before the trend becomes irreversible.
answers.additionalContext: Meridian.tech is currently focused on solidifying its position against local brokers and emerging global competitors by optimizing operational efficiency rather than aggressive market share acquisition.
answers.teamSize: Our digital and innovation organization includes 80+ professionals across centers of excellence for AI/ML, cloud engineering, UX design, and agile delivery. We run an internal incubator program that has graduated 6 new digital products to market in the past 2 years, alongside a corporate venture capital arm that makes strategic minority investments in relevant startups.

opportunities.title: Enhance Digital Self-Service (CX Optimization)
opportunities.rationale: Directly addresses customer churn feedback by streamlining the claims and policy management process via an improved self-service portal. This is a high-leverage, low-risk move that aligns with market defense by improving mid-tier retention.

first_actions: Audit current self-service friction points (time to claim/update policy).
Define MVP scope for 'easy claims submission' workflow.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduce average time from claim notification to payment confirmation by 25% within 3 months.
milestones: Q2: Beta launch with 50 pilot users
Q3: Full rollout and performance monitoring

opportunities.title: Expand Product Portfolio into Heat Stress Insurance
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging existing satellite and weather data infrastructure, Meridian.tech can expand its coverage to include heat stress insurance for livestock. This is a bold move that diversifies the risk profile beyond pure rainfall events, creating a new competitive moat in the European Insurtech space.

first_actions: Conduct feasibility study on required sensor integration and data modeling.
Identify regulatory approval pathways for new product lines.
execution_plan.success_metric: Successful pilot launch of Heat Stress Insurance with a 5% initial uptake rate.
milestones: Q1: Detailed technical requirements and risk modeling complete
Q3: Internal product approval for regulatory filing
Q6: Commercial soft launch in Portugal

next_steps.action: Establish cross-functional task force to define CX modernization roadmap.
Initiate feasibility study for heat stress insurance, including data requirements and regulatory assessment.

key_weaknesses: Organizational inertia in adopting new agile practices across non-tech departments.
Lack of formalized, cohesive strategy linking innovation output directly to specific market defense objectives.
High reliance on senior executive sponsorship which risks bottlenecks when aligning diverse divisional needs.
